newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rail traffic up sharply this week vs year ago.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rail traffic up sharply this week vs year ago.

text.p: Bad weather at this time last year made for a sharp increase in the current weekly volume of U.S. rail freight traffic compared to a year ago, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.

AAR said traffic volume on major railroads as measured in ton-miles rose 14.3 percent in the week ended February 8 to 27.2 billion ton-miles from 23.8 billion in the same week last year. A ton-mile equals one ton of freight hauled one mile.
The railroad group attributed much of the increase to severe winter weather that hampered traffic at this time last year.
"Traffic last year was affected by severe winter wheather in much of the country," a AAR official Craig Rockney said.

New carloads rose 14.1 percent in the week ended February 8 to 345,810 from 303,077 in the year-ago week. The number of new trailers and containers rose 8.7 percent to 164,765 from 151,535 a year earlier.
AAR said traffic in most all of the major commodity groups was up from the year-ago week.

Among the largest gains were loadings of stone, clay and glass products, up 24.8 percent from last year; coal, up 22 percent; metallic ores, up 15.4 percent; lumber and wood products, up 14.3 percent; and chemicals, up 12.9 percent.

AAR also said traffic was up sharply on Canada's two transcontinental railroads in the latest week. It said the number of new trailers and containers totaled 24,346, up 4.2 percent from the same week last year. New carloadings totaled 53,029, a 9.5 percent increase from last year.
